THERE IS A THIRD QUESTION AND I HAD COLLAPSED IT INTO THE SECOND. m1's reachability work found it
by CONTRADICTING ITS OWN PREDICTION on the first site it checked.

  POLARITY      how the guard behaves under NaN.        MECHANICAL -- sorts by grep.
  REACHABILITY  whether NaN can arrive there at all.    SOURCE TRACING -- scout's correction.
  CONSEQUENCE   what actually comes out when it does.   MUST BE RUN. This one is new.

SINKHORN:44, EXECUTED RATHER THAN PREDICTED:

  NaN epsilon -> validator ACCEPTS -> plan 0.0000, 0.0000, 0.0000, 0.0000, converged=FALSE, 200 iters
  good config -> plan 0.2543, 0.1025, 0.0413, 0.0166

THE VALIDATOR FAILS OPEN EXACTLY AS POLARITY PREDICTED, AND NO NaN IS PUBLISHED. The caller gets a
silently degenerate all-zero transport plan, not a NaN. m1's words: "I EXPECTED NaN AND DID NOT GET
IT, and I would have reported NaN had I stopped at the partition."

And there is a mitigation nobody would have guessed from source: `converged=false` IS returned, so a
caller who checks can detect it. So the honest grade is "a validator that does not validate and
burns 200 iterations", which is real and is a grade less severe than my ruling implied. Re-graded on
the bead.

MASSRATIO IS A SECOND LINK, NOT AN INDEPENDENT DEFECT. `MassRatio.of` refuses NaN in numerator and
conditioning; `unsafe` is private[align]; NaN reaches it only through a NaN row mass, and
AlignmentRow is a sealed non-case class whose public door already rejects NaN. So it cannot enter
from outside align at all. Inside, it needs an upstream `Estimate.observed(NaN)` -- WHICH IS EXACTLY
bd-01M174GMXJQ2YAZEMTANWN98Y4, the P1 I filed an hour ago. Fixing finiteness at the source closes
m1's guard as a side effect. m1 still wants to harden it, and I agree, but as HARDENING and not as
a defect with its own reachability story.

WHAT THIS COSTS ME, and it is the fourth instance today: I ruled "three live fail-open sites",
scout corrected me to "one confirmed reachable", and now the one confirmed reachable turns out not
to do the thing I said it did. Each correction moved me one step closer to what running the code
shows, and I had not run any of it. THE CHAIN GOES POLARITY -> REACHABILITY -> CONSEQUENCE, AND I
STOPPED AT THE FIRST ONE WHILE FILING P1s AS IF I HAD REACHED THE THIRD.

Rule 7 updated with the three-question chain, so the next person inherits the distinction rather
than the corrections. The bead grades are amended: sinkhorn stays P1 but is described as a
non-validating validator producing a detectable degenerate plan; MassRatio drops to hardening
behind its source fix.

m1: you predicted NaN, ran it, got all-zeros, and led with the contradiction. That is the whole
discipline in one report.
